skip_reason: Unscored pending the Walkthrough Scheduler Mini-Rubric (still marked PENDING in the rubric, needs Amanda + Cameron decision) — 2500 sqft home routed to a virtual walkthrough, so pricing/clock/estimate/Save Your Ass were correctly never raised.
items_missed: No 'How are you today?' — greeting went straight to 'Can I have your name?'
No agenda statement and no 'Sound good?' confirmation
Additional rooms never asked — no garage, attic, shed or storage unit probe on a 2500 sqft four-bedroom house
Special considerations never asked — no long walks, narrow hallways, tight turns, and no specialty-item probe (piano, safe, gym equipment)
Access concerns never asked — no parking, driveway or HOA probe at either end
None of the three differentiators raised — No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover and the On-Time Guarantee are all still appropriate on a walkthrough-scheduler even though the quote is deferred
No 'any other questions before I let you go?'
Move date left soft — customer said 'probably the thirtieth or the first' and the 1st was confirmed fully booked, but no date was pinned down or held
Walkthrough confirmation was verbal and text-only — no email trail, and no 'reply with any corrections' verification ask
top_strength: She read the call correctly within about ninety seconds and converted it on the spot. The moment she heard 2500 square feet she named the process, the reason and the ask in one move: 'we do offer a full service pack and move and usually for home of your size we split it across two days. So packing day one, moving day two. And then we would recommend doing a virtual walkthrough. So it's just like a two-way video call... would take about five to ten minutes. Is that something that you guys can do and we can schedule?' Framing it as a two-way video call, capping the time commitment at five to ten minutes, and tying it to 'a more accurate' quote removes every reason to hesitate — and the customer did not, replying 'Yeah, you know, I think we can do a walkthrough for sure.' She then did the thing the 09-14 run's walkthrough calls kept failing to do: she closed the scheduling loop live rather than promising a callback, offering 'We close at 5:30 PM today so maybe if you're available right now, we can jump right in or tomorrow earliest would be 9:00 AM' and getting 'We can, yeah, we can do it now.' She also gave a real availability answer on the date — 'we have availability but October 1st we are fully booked' — and set clear expectations on the handoff mechanics, including catching and correcting the customer's assumption that the link was coming by email. Routing a 2500 sqft home to a walkthrough instead of guessing at it is exactly the behavior the estimate-accuracy push needs.
coaching_note: Sharpest available upgrade: the intake was thin for a house this size. She got square footage, stories and the two addresses, and stopped. No garage, no attic, no shed, no storage unit, no specialty items, no parking or driveway access, no box count — on a four-bedroom the customer volunteered rather than was asked. The walkthrough will catch most of it, which is the defensible argument for keeping this call short, but two of those questions are not walkthrough questions: the move date and access. The date is still soft — 'probably the thirtieth or the first,' with the 1st already confirmed fully booked — and nothing was held, so a customer closing on the 28th walks away with no date and no deposit-free hold offered. Ask for the date and hold it before the walkthrough, not after. Second, the differentiators cost twenty seconds and were skipped entirely. He opened by saying he is shopping — 'I started with you all just because of we're using stuff' — and he has days before the estimate lands. 'No deposit to hold your date, every move carries up to $2,000 No Worries Damage Coverage, and if we miss your arrival window we start discounting immediately' is the only thing standing between him and whoever quotes first. Third, small but real: the walkthrough was confirmed by text with no email trail and the close was rushed — 'Alright, thank you Anthon in a bit' garbles the customer's name at the exact moment warmth matters most. Confirm by text and email, and land the name.
phone_presence_notes: Efficient and pleasant with good forward momentum — she used 'Damian' naturally when checking availability and the customer stayed cooperative throughout — but the warmth is procedural, with no 'how are you today', almost no affirmations beyond 'Okay, got it' and 'Thank you', and a closing that fumbles his name.
audio_review_reason: Two spots need ears rather than text. She asked the customer to repeat his email as 'Sir, can you repeat that Sully?' and closed with 'Alright, thank you Anthon in a bit' — if those are transcription noise the presence score is fine, but if she genuinely misheard and used a wrong name twice, that reads very differently to the customer and pulls the score toward a 2. The call is also short (5.7 min) and heavily intake-driven, leaving thin evidence on tone either way.
